angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 586,788 km at 180.17 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5504 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 1.43): 180.17 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.84345 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TIC 178172313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 586,788 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.933 (0.892 to 0.973) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5405.59 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TIC 178172313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TIC 178172313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/tic-178172313.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.556, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TIC 178172313 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.29608, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5052420929392289024, flags_flame 00: age_flame 0.92173463 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 0.2 to 2.3648887)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
